transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-12
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Mark Rivera (Nova CTO), Sara Kwon (Nova ML), Diego Morales (Nova Product)

Auto-summary: demo of Redwood Optimize quantization profiles (INT8/FP8), quality vs latency tradeoffs, benchmark plan and next steps.

---
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh I'm Alex from Redwood, I'm the owner on this account. Priya and I will run through a quick Optimize walkthrough focused on quant profiles, we know Nova's latency constraints, so we'll focus on quality versus latency.
[00:18] Mark: Yep thanks, excited to see the numbers. Our goal is a P95 around 200 milliseconds on inference for short prompts, and we want to avoid any regressions in answer quality for our core workflows.
[00:28] Priya: great, that's helpful. Quick agenda: 1) brief remind of quant profiles (INT8, FP8), 2) demo the Optimize console charts and recommended profiles, 3) discuss benchmarking methodology and pilot plan.
[00:40] Diego: sounds good, and just to confirm, are we talking hosted or dedicated for the pilot?
[00:46] Alex: likely Dedicated, given your throughput and data isolation asks, but we'll show both hosted baselines and what Dedicated looks like.
[00:54] Sara: also, curious about metrics — semantic similarity vs token-level perplexity — what do you usually use?
[01:02] Priya: we typically run both. For semantic we use embedding-based cosine similarity and a human-eval spot-check for the top deciles; perplexity is noisy across quant configs but is a useful signal.

[02:10] Priya: ok jumping into the console, I'm sharing my screen — bear with the screen share lag. So here's Redwood Optimize, this is the quantization profiles view. You'll see default profiles for INT8, FP8 and a few hybrid options.
[02:28] Mark: can you explain the difference again, quick? INT8 for cost, FP8 for quality?
[02:35] Priya: yeah in simple terms INT8 typically gives best throughput/cost but can impact some quality characteristics, FP8 sits in the middle — better numeric fidelity than int8 for some models so you see fewer hallucinations on certain tasks. But it's model dependent.
[02:50] Alex: and we include a per-model recommendation. For example, for the 7B-ish family we often see INT8 hits almost parity on many tasks, but on code tasks or long-context summarization FP8 sometimes preserves quality.

[03:20] Priya: here's a common chart — quality vs latency. X-axis is latency (P95 ms), Y-axis is semantic-similarity (normalized). Each dot is a profile run: blue=FP8, orange=INT8, green=baseline FP16. You can see INT8 moves left (lower latency) but some tasks dip in similarity.
[03:43] Sara: I see. The dots have error bars — what's that?
[03:46] Priya: those represent run variance across our eval set. We run 10 seeds or bootstraps to estimate stability.
[03:55] Mark: what about KV cache and batching? That will impact our P95 quite a bit, right?
[04:01] Priya: yes — two big levers. KV cache reduces repeated compute on long contexts, batching increases throughput but adds latency depending on batching window. For Nova's 200ms P95 target we usually enable small batching (2-4) and aggressive KV caching for prefixes.

[05:12] Alex: quick interruption — Mark, can you remind us of your typical prompt length and concurrency?
[05:18] Mark: median prompt length is 80 tokens, tail up to 600 for long conversation. Peak concurrent requests around 180 QPS during spikes.
[05:28] Priya: perfect, that explains the Dedicated recommendation. For 180 QPS with 200ms P95 we model bin-packing of gpus, and INT8 gives a ~1.7x token throughput improvement in our microbench, FP8 ~1.3x versus FP16 baseline.

[06:00] Priya: on this next slide you can see model-level breakdowns. For model A (7B variant) INT8 had 97.5% semantic similarity vs FP16 baseline and reduced P95 from 280ms to 160ms. For model B (13B-ish) INT8 dropped similarity to 92% on code tasks, FP8 kept it at 96%.
[06:33] Sara: that's the kind of number we need. Our threshold is 95% similarity on the 1k prompt eval set.
[06:40] Priya: so recommendation: run a targeted INT8 pilot on model A for your chat flows and FP8 for longer summarization/code flows. We're also able to create hybrid routing rules — traffic split by route.

[07:05] Diego: practically, how do you measure semantic similarity? Are you using embeddings from the same model?
[07:12] Priya: we use a stable embedding model, separate from the generative model, to avoid model-aliasing. Cosine similarity with a calibrated threshold, plus human spot checks for edge cases.

[07:44] Alex: quick note: there are some rumbling edge cases with int8 where tokenization and activation-clipping create small shifts in completion style — these are usually caught by our regression harness.
[07:58] Mark: what about safety and hallucination rates after quant? Any change?
[08:04] Priya: generally quantization itself doesn't change safety policies; hallucination rates can move slightly if numeric fidelity affects the model's knowledge retrieval, so we recommend pairing quant with post-qa checks and reranking.

[09:10] Priya: ok demoing the benchmark spreadsheet — this is what we'll share: rows for prompt id, metric columns for semantic sim, perplexity, token latency, cost estimate; filters for profile and batch size. We'll fill in your 1k prompts and show delta between INT8/FP8.
[09:35] Diego: will you run it on our data in our VPC?
[09:38] Alex: for pilot we can run in Redwood Dedicated in your VPC or private cluster depending on contract — data never leaves your tenancy. We'll need the eval set and security contact, and we can bring the job to your environment.

[10:20] Mark: security questions: SOC2, KMS, audit logs — do you have those?
[10:26] Alex: yes SOC2 Type II, KMS integrations (AWS, GCP, Azure), audit logs available in the Console; we'll share the security pack after this call.
[10:34] Mark: great, please send.

[11:00] Priya: so now a short live demo of latency profiling — I'm toggling INT8 profile and running a small synthetic. Notice P95 drop, and the output differences highlighted in red on the right. Some of the stylistic tokens change but semantic picks up.
[11:25] Sara: I see a few truncated outputs in INT8 run on longer context — is that expected?
[11:30] Priya: that might be tokenization boundary issues or beam stopping differences; we'll include stop-token tuning in the pilot.

[12:15] Alex: competitor question — Mark any preference or concern around using Redwood vs say OpenAI or Anthropic in your stack?
[12:23] Mark: just cost and control. We like Redwood's dedicated options and the ability to run on-prem later.
[12:30] Alex: good to know.

[13:02] Priya: circling back to quality vs latency, here's a recommended mapping: chat route -> INT8 on model A; long-summary route -> FP8 or FP16; fallback policy to FP16 if similarity drops below threshold. We can automate rollouts and canary with automatic rollback.
[13:28] Diego: how slow is rollback? If something breaks mid-rollout, we need instant fallback.
[13:33] Priya: rollbacks are near-instant because we keep the FP16 pool warmed and route via smart routing. In practice we see <30s to failover for traffic.

[14:05] Mark: what about costs? If INT8 is 1.7x throughput, does that translate linearly to 1.7x cost savings?
[14:12] Alex: roughly yes on tokens processed, but effective savings depend on your batching, cache hit rates, and reserved capacity discounts. We'll provide modeled cost scenarios in the spreadsheet.

[15:00] Priya: quick note on quantization technicals — INT8 here is per-channel symmetric quant with per-layer clipping; FP8 is block floating with mantissa/exponent tuning. Both have tradeoffs re: kernel complexity and GPU support.
[15:22] Sara: Wait, FP-eight isn't widely supported on all hardware, right?
[15:26] Priya: correct — FP8 support depends on the GPU and runtime; for Dedicated we ensure the kernel path and fallback are validated. If hardware doesn't support FP8 we use a compatible emulation or choose INT8/FP16.

[16:10] Priya: ok moving on — benchmark plan proposal: 1) run 1k-prompt baseline FP16 in hosted to get baseline numbers, 2) run INT8/FP8 in Dedicated with KV cache/batching aligned to your production config, 3) evaluate semantic sim, perplexity, latency and cost. Target deliverable: table with recommended profile per route.
[16:40] Mark: timeline?
[16:43] Alex: we can kick the pilot as soon as NDA + eval set + security contact are confirmed; estimated 2 weeks to run and validate.

[17:10] Diego: any manual tuning required? For instance, quant fine-tuning per layer?
[17:16] Priya: sometimes we do per-layer calibration and small amount of quant-aware calibration (no retraining usually) — it's part of the Optimize toolkit and we can automate most of it.

[18:05] Sara: will the SDK flags be simple to flip? i.e. model=xxx, profile=int8, kv_cache=true?
[18:10] Alex: yes, trivial to flip, and we store profile configs in the Console for rollouts.

[18:45] Priya: ok a couple of quick gotchas: 1) tokenization drift when quant changes 2) small output style shifts 3) model-specific behavior — so the regression harness is important.

[19:20] Mark: what's the expected human-eval overhead? We'll need people to review a sample of outputs.
[19:25] Priya: for 1k prompts we usually human-eval the top 50 edge cases flagged by low sim score, takes ~1-2 days for a small review team.

[20:00] Alex: let's go through the proposed next steps — quick recap. We'll send the spreadsheet, priya will run benchmark, mark will provide eval set and security contact and sign NDA. Anything missing?
[20:15] Diego: can you include cost modelling for peak vs steady?
[20:19] Alex: yes will include steady vs peak scenarios.

[20:40] Mark: quick note: our procurement wants vendor security docs and a preliminary SOW.
[20:46] Alex: we'll attach the security pack and a draft SOW to the email.

[21:05] Priya: ok I'm going to demo one more thing — quality diagnostics — this shows token-level differences and highlights tokens that changed due to quantization, gives a quick heuristic for whether the change is meaningful.
[21:30] Sara: that's useful.

[22:00] Alex: we're at about 22 minutes in the call; I'll skip some demo screens and jump to Q&A to respect your time.
[22:10] Mark: thanks.

[22:45] Sara: couple of final questions: 1) can we set hard SLOs and alarms inside Console? 2) is there support for model pinning per route?
[22:55] Priya: yes to both, you can define SLOs and alert thresholds; model pinning is supported and we have rollout policies per route.

[23:30] Mark: ok I'm satisfied. We'll aim to get the eval set and security contact this week.
[23:38] Alex: great. Priya anything to add?
[23:41] Priya: just that we'll include a canary plan and auto rollback suggestion in the runbook.

[24:00] Diego: and will you share the raw logs from the pilot? We need token-level traces for debug.
[24:05] Priya: yes, we can provide sanitized token traces in your VPC, and raw traces with PII redaction if needed.

[24:40] Alex: alright we're going to close with a recap and action items.
[25:00] Alex: ACTIONS: Alex send spreadsheet/security pack/SOW; Priya run pilot and share runbook; Mark provide eval set/NDA/security contact.

[25:30] Mark: sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[25:35] Priya: thanks all.
[25:40] Alex: we'll follow up with calendar invite for the pilot kickoff and rough ETA.
